theBlocker.what: Nebraska CC 6:12 composes its own caption with form JavaScript, and the two facts that caption needs cannot be bound by the shared semantics.
measuredFromThePinnedBinary: `TYPEOFCOURTRESULTS` ships carrying the source value 'IN THE                   COURT OF' and `fullcountystatementRIGHT` ships carrying '                            COUNTY, NEBRASKA '. Those are the caption scaffolding, drawn from the widgets' own values, and they flatten as ink.

`enter the type of court` and `enter the county` are BOTH HIDDEN -- annotation flag 2 -- and both carry instructional source text, '(Enter the type of court)' and '(Enter the county name)'. A write into either is invisible ink, and this cohort's builders assert against exactly that.
the two visible controls that set the caption are dropdowns, `TYPEOFCOURTDROPDOWN` and `DROPDOWNCOUNTY2`, and the form's JavaScript is what copies a choice into the results field.
theBlocker.whyTheCountyCannotBeWritten: `DROPDOWNCOUNTY2` carries all ninety-three Nebraska counties as exact options, so the value exists and would match. But decideBinding refuses it with no_allowlisted_fact_matches: the descriptor for matter.county matches /\bcounty\b/ and the name DROPDOWNCOUNTY2 has no word boundary around COUNTY. An explicit mapping cannot rescue it either -- the finalizer requires a descriptor to match the name BEFORE an explicit mapping is consulted, so explicitMappings can only narrow a binding that already exists, never create one.
theBlocker.whyTheCourtCannotBeWritten: `TYPEOFCOURTRESULTS` does bind matter.court, but writing into it would replace the printed caption fragment 'IN THE ___ COURT OF' with a bare court name and break the sentence the caption is made of.
theBlocker.whyTheEmailCannotBeWritten: `emailaddress` does not bind: the descriptor matches /\be[-\s]?mail\b/ and the name has no word boundary. This is a fact the platform HOLDS, on a field Nebraska Supreme Court Rule 2-208 REQUIRES a self-represented party to complete.

whatThisLaneDidNotDoAboutIt: It did not declare the e-mail address required-before-filing. That disposition's first condition is that the platform holds no value for the fact, and the platform holds this one. The mechanical check would have passed -- no other field on the document carries the label -- and passing it would have been a false statement in the field map.

It did not add descriptors to scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-field-semantics.mjs for `emailaddress`, `DROPDOWNCOUNTY2` or `citystatezip`-style names. That list is shared by every family in the factory and widening a match is how a fact starts binding somewhere nobody looked; it needs its own author and its own mutation tests.
It did not write into either hidden widget, and did not write the county through the results field.
rows.whatWouldUnblockIt: three descriptor additions in the shared field semantics, made deliberately by its owner with mutation tests: a name-channel match for `emailaddress`, one for `DROPDOWNCOUNTY2` (or an explicit-mapping path that does not require a prior descriptor match), and a decision about whether a JavaScript-composed caption field should be written at all. With those, both Nebraska families in this cohort are straightforward builds.
rows.alsoWorthRecording: the route is pardon-then-seal and CC 6:12 item 2 asks the participant to select one of four dispositions, the third of which is 'Resulted in a conviction that was later pardoned'. That IS the route, and the packet could not state it: the shared finalizer does not write checkboxes, so a route-determined election has to be carried to the participant with an instruction naming the exact box. Worth a decision from whoever owns the finalizer, because the same limitation applies to every family whose route is expressed as a tick.
